title: My Boy
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Satoko Tawada, a 30-year-old office worker hurt by her boss and former lover, meets 12-year-old Mashu Hayami practicing soccer alone in a park and begins coaching him. Both are lonely, and Mashu's home life with a high-handed, uninvolved father is troubled. When his father objects to their bond she is transferred away; years later they reunite, Mashu confesses and is turned down because she is an adult and he a child, and Satoko faces that she simply wants to be by his side.
life_message: Two lonely people can give each other refuge, but the story leaves open, and troubling, what that bond should become.

content.note: Emotionally intense, ambiguous bond between an adult woman and a boy who later confesses love (Wikipedia; MU Age Gap, Student-Adult Relationship). Volume 1 is non-romantic per AIPT; sexual content not reported.
Loneliness, emotional numbness and a neglectful home after the mother's death (AIPT; Wikipedia; MU Negligent Parents).
An adult forming a private close bond with a child outside his family; the father's complaint gets her transferred (Wikipedia).

frames.concerns: Romantic longing between an adult and a minor is left sympathetically ambiguous; parental authority bypassed.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor conflicts; disputes go to the employer, who transfers Satoko.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Satoko follows her heart against social and parental objections.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family neglect versus chosen bond; Satoko's sister supports her.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Father's and boss's authority shown as harsh or self-serving.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern urban office life, no religious frame.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Emotional need and personal fulfillment drive choices.

folkways.japan: Workplace transfers as discipline, cram schools and office-lady life reflect Japanese corporate and school norms.

delivery.evidence: AIPT praises restraint and foreshadowing that is not heavy-handed.
delivery.note: The story withholds judgment and lets readers weigh the relationship themselves.

winners_losers: Satoko and Mashu are both sympathetic; Mashu's father and Satoko's ex-boss are cast as self-serving authority figures.
to_verify: Whether the relationship becomes romantic or physical after the time skip, and how the ending frames it.
